The target saves $ra in $t5 around each jal (addu t5,ra,zero ... addu ra,t5,zero), passes the 2nd return value through $v1 from $t1 or $a1 (addu v1,t1,zero / addu v1,a1,zero) with v0 set to 0 (xor) or a0 (addu), and fills delay slots with nops. No C expression produces the $ra save/restore around a call, so this is not reachable by compiled C.

claude-haiku-5-5-24.why: Target is 8 instructions: bnez a2 -> j func_800422F8 (taken) / j func_800423F4 (fall-through), with 3 trailing nops. Tail calls via bare `j` with no frame. Four C variants (void/s32 returns, typed and unprototyped callees, arg-forwarding) all compiled to a frame (addiu sp / sw ra) with jal, and gcc 2.7.2 does not emit sibling-call `j`. Also the following code at .L80042650 saves ra in $t5 (move $t5,$ra; jal; move $ra,$t5), which is hand-written asm style, not gcc output. Likely hand-written assembly; the second block at 0x80042650 looks like a separate function.

claude-haiku-5-5-22.why: Likely hand-written assembly, not C. The entry is a bare 'bnez a2; j func_800423F4 / j func_800422F8' dispatch with no frame, and the following code saves ra in $t5 (move $t5,$ra; jal; move $ra,$t5) and returns through $t1/$a1 registers, which gcc 2.7.2 doesn't emit. The C candidate (void f(s32) calling both) scored 2130-2230 with a stack frame that the target lacks. Recommend treating as asm.

claude-opus-medium-1.why: This is hand-written KMC libgcc 64-bit div/mod dispatch. It tail-jumps (j) to func_800423F4/func_800422F8, has nop padding, and has a second entry at .L80042650 that saves ra in $t5 (`addu t5,ra,zero; jal; addu ra,t5,zero`) and returns the result in t1/a0/a1. That is a non-ABI convention GCC doesn't emit.
